blocks.html: A database (DB), at its core, is a logically organized collection of data—stored, structured, and maintained to allow efficient retrieval, updates, and management.
blocks.text: A database (DB), at its core, is a logically organized collection of data—stored, structured, and maintained to allow efficient retrieval, updates, and management.

blocks.html: There is no single, universally agreed-upon definition of what a database is.

blocks.html: What’s important to remember is that not everything that stores data qualifies as a database.
blocks.text: What’s important to remember is that not everything that stores data qualifies as a database.

blocks.html: What makes storage a database is the presence of a defined set of rules that determine how data is organized and made usable.
blocks.text: What makes storage a database is the presence of a defined set of rules that determine how data is organized and made usable.

blocks.html: These rules must be enforced by a system that manages the database by ensuring consistency, integrity, and efficient access to the data, which is called Database Management System (DBMS).
